name: Reachy Mini
notes: Desktop expressive robot. Lite kit ($299) or full autonomous version ($449) with onboard compute + battery. Camera + mic array + speaker means it does conversation, gesture recognition, and CV out of the box. Fully open hardware + software.

name: Crazyflie 2.1+
notes: Open-source nano-drone. Stack expansion decks (Lighthouse positioning, Multi-ranger, AI-deck with camera) for autonomous flight, swarms, indoor positioning. Used in research and education widely.

name: M5Stack Core2
notes: All-in-one ESP32 dev kit with touchscreen, audio, RTC, battery in a finished case. Modular base and HAT ecosystem. Best 'just works out of the box' option for IoT prototypes.

name: Adafruit MagTag
capabilities: magnets on the back (snap to fridge / wall)
notes: Magnetic e-paper display you slap on the fridge. CircuitPython supported. Batteries last weeks. Drop-in replacement for the 'Pi + Waveshare HAT' build if you want it pre-assembled.

name: Pimoroni Tufty 2040
notes: Tiny RP2040 board with built-in color LCD. Works as a conference badge, status display, or generative-art frame. Cheap enough to build many.

name: PineTime
software_stack: Companion apps for Linux / Android / iOS
notes: Open-source smartwatch under $30. Default firmware (InfiniTime) is mature; Wasp-OS adds a Python runtime if you want to write watchfaces in micropython. Pebble's spiritual successor.

name: PocketBeagle 2
notes: Pi Zero alternative with REAL-TIME hardware (PRUs) for motor control, signal generation, hard-deadline I/O. Open hardware down to the schematic.

name: LimeSDR Mini 2.0
notes: Open-source software-defined radio. Receive AND transmit (where legal) from 10MHz to 3.5GHz. ADS-B aircraft tracking, GSM eavesdropping (with SIM), LoRa testing, GPS spoofing for testing. Premium price; serious capability.

name: iRobot Create 3
notes: Mobile robot platform built on Roomba i-series chassis. Subscribe to /odom, publish to /cmd_vel — drive it. Used widely in education + research. Indoor only.

name: TurtleBot 4 Lite
notes: Full ROS 2 mobile robot kit: Create 3 + Pi 4 + lidar + stereo cam. Comes ready for SLAM + autonomous navigation out of the box. Price reflects the full sensor stack.

name: LeRobot SO-ARM100
capabilities: follower or leader mode for teleop
notes: DIY-buildable open-source robot arm, the canonical LeRobot teaching platform. Sourced as kit/parts from various sellers. Used for imitation learning research with HuggingFace datasets.

name: Pimoroni Inky Frame 5.7"
notes: Self-contained 7-color e-paper picture frame with Pico W aboard — no separate Pi needed. Pulls images from any URL on a Wi-Fi schedule. The 7.3" sibling is similar; 5.7" is the desk-friendly size.

name: M5StickC Plus 2
notes: Pocket-sized ESP32 with screen + IMU + battery in a finished case. Good for wearable badges, status indicators, motion-triggered devices. Newer V2 fixes the V1 quirks.

name: M5Stack Cardputer
software_stack: BadUSB / payload mode for security testing
notes: Credit-card-sized ESP32 with a real keyboard and screen. Used for portable hacking, BadUSB, mini-terminals, ham radio control. The keyboard makes it usable as a standalone device, not just a dev kit.

name: Adafruit Feather ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT
capabilities: 240x135 color TFT on the BOTTOM (so it shows on a desk)
compatible with all Feather-form-factor add-on boards
notes: Most popular Adafruit ESP32 dev board. Reverse TFT means the screen faces you when the board sits flat on a desk. Pairs with the entire FeatherWing accessory ecosystem.

name: Pimoroni Enviro Indoor
notes: Battery-powered indoor air-quality sensor with built-in OLED status. Publishes to MQTT, Adafruit IO, or Home Assistant. Configurable wake/sleep cadence to last weeks on a charge.

name: OpenMV Cam H7 Plus
capabilities: shield ecosystem (LCD, FLIR thermal, WiFi, LoRa)
software_stack: QR / AprilTag / barcode / face / line / blob detection libraries
notes: Open-source machine-vision camera. Run image-classification models, AprilTag detection, line-following — all in MicroPython on the device, no Pi/desktop needed. Battery-friendly.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3
capabilities: Sense variant adds OV2640 camera + microphone
notes: Cheapest credible ESP32-S3 dev board. The Sense variant ($14) adds a camera + mic — turning it into a $14 vision module. Common in wearable + always-on projects.

name: SO-ARM101 6-Axis Robotic Arm
notes: 3D-printed 6-DOF robotic arm designed for HuggingFace LeRobot. Leader-follower teleoperation kit for imitation learning. Includes 30kg torque bus servos, magnetic encoders, and gripper-mounted camera mount. Works out-of-box with LeRobot record/train/deploy pipeline. Requires 3D printing (STL provided) unless buying assembled. Multiple vendors: Waveshare ($90 parts), Seeed ($235 kit), Hiwonder ($440 assembled).

name: Koch v1.1 Low-Cost Robot Arm
notes: Low-cost 6-DOF robotic arm using Robotis Dynamixel XL330/XL430 servos. Leader-follower teleoperation pair for under $500 total. Direct integration with HuggingFace LeRobot ML pipeline for dataset recording and policy training. 3D-printed hardware design (STL files in original repo). Pre-assembled TwinArm sets also available from WowRobo. Supports folding clothes, grasping objects, and drawer opening tasks.

name: Petoi Bittle Robot Dog
notes: Open-source quadruped robot dog kit. 8-DOF (2 per leg), NyBoard V1 controller, 1-hour playtime. Pre-programmed with 35+ lifelike movements. Programmable via block-based coding, Python, C++, or Arduino. Optional Raspberry Pi and camera modules for AI vision tasks. Mobile app and Bluetooth remote control. STEM curriculum included. Assembles in ~1 hour. MIT-licensed OpenCat firmware.

name: Petoi Nybble Robot Cat
notes: Open-source quadruped robot cat, the original OpenCat platform. Wooden frame + acrylic body. NyBoard V1 with Arduino compatibility. 11 DOF including head and tail. Programmable via block coding, Python, C++, or Arduino IDE. Optional ultrasonic sensor for distance detection and LED programming. Mobile app control via Bluetooth. STEM education focused with free coding curriculum. Build time 3-4 hours.

name: Mini Pupper 2 Quadruped Robot
notes: ROS 2 quadruped robot inspired by Stanford Pupper. Pre-assembled kit with 12x CLS6336HV servos, Raspberry Pi 4B, Ubuntu 22.04. Optional STL-06P LiDAR for SLAM/navigation and Pi camera v2 for computer vision. Supports walking gaits, obstacle avoidance, and OpenCV-based gesture control. Web-based calibration. 1-hour assembly for pre-assembled kit. Full ROS 2 simulation in Gazebo.

name: Pimoroni Inky Frame 5.7"
capabilities: Raspberry Pi Pico W onboard 2.4GHz WiFi
notes: 7-color ACeP e-paper photo frame powered by Pico W. Pre-flashed MicroPython with WiFi examples (NASA APOD, news, jokes). 30-sec refresh. Deep-sleep RTC wakes at 20uA for months of battery life. 2x Qw/ST ports for sensor breakouts. 8MB PSRAM. Ideal for always-on dashboards, art frames, and conference badges.

name: LILYGO T-Display S3
notes: Compact ESP32-S3 dev board with 1.9-inch color TFT. I8080 parallel interface for fast refresh. Non-soldered and soldered pin versions. Optional touch and acrylic shell variants. Arduino/PlatformIO libs include TFT_eSPI and LVGL examples. JST-GH 1.25mm battery connector. WiFi+BLE for connected displays.

name: LILYGO T-Display S3 AMOLED Plus
notes: ESP32-S3 with vibrant AMOLED display. Individual pixel illumination for true blacks and high contrast. Plus variant adds RTC, PMU, SD card slot, and battery holder. QSPI interface for fast screen updates. Supports touch input. Self-illuminating pixels work well in dark environments. Arduino/PlatformIO/MicroPython all supported.

name: LILYGO T5 4.7" e-Paper V2.3
notes: Large high-res e-paper dev board with ESP32-S3. 16 grayscale levels for photo-quality images. 540x960 resolution at 4.7 inches. RTC for scheduled wake/sleep. SD card for image caching. EPDiy library provides optimized parallel e-ink driving. Good for weather stations, e-readers, price tags, and info panels. Battery connector for portable use.

name: M5Stack M5Paper V1.1
notes: Pocket-sized programmable e-ink tablet with touch. 235 ppi 16-shade grayscale for crisp text and images. 1150mAh battery lasts weeks with RTC wake. 3 expansion ports connect to M5Stack sensor ecosystem. Pre-installed apps include calculator, weather, e-book reader. M5Unified/M5GFX libs provide display, audio, power, IMU abstraction. Good for smart remote, info panel, e-reader.

name: M5Stack M5StickC PLUS2
notes: Thumb-sized ESP32 dev kit with color TFT. Wearable form factor with lanyard/watch accessories. BMI270 IMU for motion sensing. IR blaster for remote control apps. Built-in mic for voice projects. M5Unified library handles display, audio, power, sensors. UIFlow blocky drag-and-drop IDE for beginners. ~120mAh battery for portable projects.

name: Pimoroni Cosmic Unicorn 32x32 LED Matrix
capabilities: Raspberry Pi Pico W onboard WiFi BLE
notes: Large square RGB LED matrix display with wireless connectivity. 1024 individually addressable squircular RGB LEDs with built-in diffusion. 300fps at 14-bit for flicker-free video recording. Onboard speaker for audio alerts. 4 buttons for mode selection. Pre-loaded MicroPython with flame, rainbow, pixel, and prompt demos. Web-based paint example lets you draw from a browser. Battery-powered for portable installations.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3 3.97" e-Paper Development Board
notes: All-in-one e-paper IoT board with voice interaction capability. 3.97-inch 800x480 e-ink with fast refresh 2.8s. Audio codec + mic enable AI voice assistant integration (DeepSeek, Doubao). Rotary switch for navigation. IMU for gesture control. PMU manages battery charging and power. TF card for media storage. Good for smart calendar, voice-enabled info panel, e-reader, weather display.

name: Adafruit SHARP Memory Display Breakout 1.3"
capabilities: retains image without power like eInk
notes: Unique hybrid between eInk and LCD. Reflective monochrome display with 168x144 resolution. Ultra-low static power draw (image retained with no power). Fast update rate unlike traditional e-paper. 3-pin SPI interface (SCK, DI, CS). Works with Adafruit GFX for drawing text, shapes, bitmaps. No backlight but daylight readable. Ideal for battery-powered wearable displays, sensor readouts, and low-power badges.

name: Adafruit Sensirion SHT40 Temperature & Humidity Sensor
notes: Fourth-gen Sensirion SHT40 with true I2C. Measures 0-75°C at ±0.2°C and 25-75% RH at ±1.8%. STEMMA QT connectors allow plug-and-play with no soldering. 3V/5V compliant. 25.5x17.7x4.8mm. Ideal for environmental monitoring, HVAC, and weather stations.

name: Adafruit BME680 Temperature, Humidity, Pressure and Gas Sensor
notes: Bosch BME680 4-in-1 environmental sensor. Measures temp (±1°C), humidity (±3%), pressure (±1 hPa absolute, usable as altimeter ±1m), and VOC gas via heated MOX sensor. Single resistance value for total VOC content. Requires 48-hour burn-in. STEMMA QT compatible. 3V/5V compliant.

name: Adafruit SCD-40 True CO2, Temperature and Humidity Sensor
notes: Sensirion SCD-40 photoacoustic true CO2 sensor (not eCO2 approximation). Range 400-2000ppm, accuracy ±(50ppm + 5% of reading). Integrated temp/humidity for compensation. I2C address 0x62. STEMMA QT. 17mA at 5s measurement rate, 0.5mA at 5min rate. Fully calibrated and linearized.

name: Adafruit AS7341 10-Channel Light / Color Sensor Breakout
notes: AMS OSRAM AS7341 multi-channel spectrometer in 3x2mm package. Detects 8 overlapping visible bands plus NIR, white, and flicker channels via SMUX multiplexer. 16-bit 6-channel ADC. Measures spectral composition more accurately than human eye. GPIO and interrupt pins. STEMMA QT. 3.3V/5V compliant.

name: Adafruit VL53L4CD Time of Flight Distance Sensor
notes: ST VL53L4CD Time-of-Flight sensor using tiny invisible laser to measure 1-1300mm distance. Detects time light takes to bounce back. Excellent for short-range proximity, object detection, and liquid-level sensing. Not affected by target color. I2C address 0x29. STEMMA QT. 25.5x17.7x4.7mm.

name: SparkFun Environmental Sensor Breakout - BME680 (Qwiic)
notes: SparkFun's Qwiic take on the Bosch BME680 4-in-1 environmental sensor. Same specs as Adafruit version: temp (±1°C), humidity (±3%), pressure (±1 hPa, altimeter-capable), and VOC gas sensing. Standard 1x1 inch Qwiic form factor. I2C broken out to Qwiic connectors and 0.1in headers. 3.3V logic.

name: SparkFun Humidity Sensor Breakout - SHTC3 (Qwiic)
notes: Sensirion SHTC3 digital humidity/temperature sensor with ±2% RH and ±0.2°C accuracy. Supply voltage 1.62V-3.6V. Very low power: 0.2uA sleep current. I2C address 0x70 (hardware-defined). Standard 1x1 inch Qwiic form factor. Qwiic connectors plus 0.1in breakout pins. Auto-detectable by OpenLog Artemis datalogger.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840 Sense
notes: Thumb-sized dev board with Nordic nRF52840 (Cortex-M4, 64MHz, 256KB RAM, 1MB Flash + 2MB onboard). BLE 5.4, NFC. Onboard LSM6DS3TR-C 6-axis IMU (accel + gyro) and PDM microphone. 5uA deep sleep. Battery charging via BQ25101. 11 digital I/O, 6 analog, 1xI2C, 1xUART, 1xSPI. Supports Arduino, CircuitPython, MicroPython. TensorFlow Lite Micro compatible.

name: M5Stack AtomS3R Development Kit
notes: Tiny 24x24x12.9mm ESP32-S3 dev kit with 8MB Flash, 8MB PSRAM. Features BMI270 6-axis IMU (0.05% accel, 0.05°/s gyro accuracy) and BMM150 3-axis magnetometer (0.3uT). 0.85-inch 128x128 color IPS display with programmable button. IR TX 12.46m range. HY2.0-4P port + 6 GPIO on bottom. USB Type-C. 3D antenna. Great for motion sensing, tiny UI projects, and IoT sensor nodes.

name: Coral USB Accelerator with Edge TPU
notes: Google Coral USB Accelerator adds an Edge TPU coprocessor via USB 3.0. Edge TPU delivers 4 TOPS (int8) at 2 TOPS/watt. Runs MobileNet v2 at ~400 FPS. Works with Debian Linux, Windows, macOS. Requires compiling TFLite models for Edge TPU. Supports image classification, object detection, pose estimation, semantic segmentation. 65x30mm USB stick form factor. Note: repo archived 2026-04-19 but hardware still sold.

name: Raspberry Pi 5
notes: Latest flagship SBC from Raspberry Pi. 2-3x faster than Pi 4. PCIe 2.0 enables NVMe SSD via M.2 HAT. In production until Jan 2036. All major OSes supported. Broadcom BCM2712 is the first RPi chip with in-house designed silicon (RP1 I/O controller). GPIO compatible with HAT ecosystem. Kernel and firmware fully open source.

name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
notes: Tiny SBC in a Raspberry Pi Zero form factor. 5x faster than original Zero. Shares 64-bit Linux ecosystem with full-size Pi boards. Ideal for embedded IoT, headless servers, and portable projects. HAT-compatible with pin header soldered. Widely available from authorized resellers globally.

name: PINE64 PinePhone Beta Edition (Convergence Package)
capabilities: Hardware kill switches (modem, WiFi/BT, mic, cameras, headphones)
notes: Open-source Linux smartphone with hardware privacy kill switches for modem, WiFi, mic, and cameras. Runs mainline Linux with community distros. Convergence package ($199) includes USB-C dock for desktop use. Original PinePhone still available; Pro model discontinued Aug 2025. Community-driven mobile Linux platform.

name: PINE64 PineTime
notes: Fully open-source smartwatch with community-developed InfiniTime firmware pre-installed. Supports OTA updates over BLE. Companion apps: Gadgetbridge (Android), Amazfish (SailfishOS/Linux), InfiniLink (iOS). Hardware schematics available. Sealed units $26.99 community price; dev kit also available for firmware developers.

name: PINE64 PineTab2
notes: Linux tablet with detachable keyboard, mainline RK3566 support, and modular repairable design. Ships with DanctNix Arch Linux + KDE Plasma. Exposed PCIe for hardware hacking. Battery, cameras, display, and eMMC are user-replaceable in ~5 min. Good mainline Linux maturity for RK3566 platform.

name: ClockworkPi uConsole
capabilities: Modular CPU system (RPi CM4 / A-04 / A-06 / RISC-V R-01)
notes: Pocket-sized modular portable computer with keyboard, trackball, and gaming controls. Accepts Raspberry Pi CM4 or ClockworkPi's own ARM/RISC-V modules. All-metal case with 3D design files on GitHub (GPL). Runs full Linux. Supports retro gaming (Pico-8, RetroArch). Popular for cyberdeck and portable terminal projects.

name: Flipper Zero
notes: Open-source portable multi-tool for pentesters and hardware hackers. Reads/emulates RFID, NFC, sub-GHz remotes, IR devices, and iButton keys. Extensible via GPIO and MicroSD. Active community firmware with apps for BadUSB, WiFi dev board, Sigrok logic analyzer, and more. Fully autonomous operation.

name: Adafruit Circuit Playground Bluefruit
notes: All-in-one educational board with sensors, LEDs, speaker, and BLE. Designed for beginners with no soldering required. Runs CircuitPython out of the box. Ten NeoPixels enable color/light projects. Capacitive touch pads support gesture input. Popular in STEM education and rapid prototyping. nRF52840 provides ample compute for wireless sensor projects.

name: BBC micro:bit V2
notes: Widely adopted educational microcontroller board used in classrooms worldwide. V2 adds speaker, microphone, and touch sensor over V1. Programs via USB drag-and-drop or wireless BLE. LED matrix doubles as a light sensor and basic display. Edge connector compatible with hundreds of expansion boards. Used by 30+ million students globally. Open-source CODAL runtime maintained by Lancaster University.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO RP2040
capabilities: 11 GPIOs (4x ADC, 2x I2C, 2x UART, 2x SPI, 1x PWM)
notes: Thumb-sized development board based on Raspberry Pi RP2040. Smallest RP2040 board available. Breadboard-friendly with castellated edges for SMT use. Supports Arduino, MicroPython, CircuitPython, and Rust. USB-C for power and programming. 4x 12-bit ADC channels. Ideal for wearable projects, sensor nodes, and space-constrained designs. Part of the XIAO ecosystem with compatible expansion boards.

name: PINE64 Pinecil
capabilities: USB-C PD 3.0 / QC 3.0 / DC 5525 barrel jack
Boost mode for temporary temperature increase
Tip sense for auto tip detection
notes: Open-source smart soldering iron running IronOS firmware on a RISC-V MCU. Heats to 400C in 6 seconds. Powers via USB-C PD, QC 3.0, or DC barrel jack. Pinecil V2 adds BLE for wireless control via PineSAM web app and USB-PD EPR 28V support. Unbrickable bootloader in ROM. Firmware updates via USB-C. Widely praised as best budget soldering iron. Compatible with TS100-style and shorter Pine64 custom tips.
